test_title: SSC CPO 2025 Official Paper (Held On: 09 Dec, 2025 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: Which of the following is a key objective of the National Health Mission (NHM)?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Child mortality reduction**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The National Health Mission (NHM) is a flagship health program by the Government of India launched in 2013 to achieve universal access to equitable, affordable, and quality healthcare services.
 
• One of its core objectives is the **reduction in child mortality** and maternal mortality rates by improving the quality of healthcare services provided at various levels.
 
• The NHM focuses on **Reproductive, Maternal, Newborn, Child, and Adolescent Health (RMNCH+A)** as a strategic approach to address key health challenges, including child mortality.
 
• Various initiatives under NHM, such as the Janani Suraksha Yojana (JSY) and Integrated Child Development Services (ICDS), aim to ensure safe deliveries and proper nutrition for children, contributing to reduced child mortality rates.
 
• NHM has significantly contributed to improving India's Infant Mortality Rate (IMR) and Under-5 Mortality Rate (U5MR) through better healthcare infrastructure and community-level interventions.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Industrial Growth**

 
 
• Industrial growth refers to the expansion of industries in terms of production, employment, and technological advancements.
 
• It is primarily driven by economic policies, investments, technological innovations, and infrastructure development.
 
• While industrial growth is critical for economic development, it is not directly related to the objectives of the NHM, which focuses on healthcare and public health services.
 
 
 
• **Space Exploration**
 
 
• Space exploration is the scientific investigation of outer space using advanced technologies such as satellites, probes, and telescopes.
 
• In India, space exploration is led by ISRO (Indian Space Research Organisation), contributing significantly to global space missions and advancements in satellite technology.
 
• This area of interest is unrelated to the NHM, which focuses on improving health outcomes rather than scientific research or space missions.
 
 
 
• **Wildlife Protection**
 
 
• Wildlife protection involves conserving ecosystems, preserving biodiversity, and safeguarding endangered species.
 
• In India, wildlife protection is governed by laws such as the Wildlife Protection Act, 1972, and initiatives like Project Tiger and Project Elephant.
 
• While wildlife protection is a significant environmental concern, it does not align with the healthcare-centric objectives of the NHM.
